items.title: How much does aggregate write-traffic raise the odds of Order #4471's race?
items.description: Order #4471's bug happened because two writes landed on the same aggregate close enough together to race. Given how many writes per second target one aggregate instance and how long each write's in-flight window lasts, this estimates the chance that at least one competing write shows up while yours is still in flight — the exact situation optimistic concurrency (the version check from L3) exists to catch. Higher traffic on a hot aggregate, or slower transactions, both push this up; a narrower aggregate boundary (fewer objects, less work per write) is one of the few levers that brings the transaction window back down.

params.name: writesPerSecond
params.label: Concurrent write attempts on this aggregate

params.name: avgTransactionMs
params.label: Average time a write stays in flight

items.compute: const windowSeconds = params.avgTransactionMs / 1000; const expectedCompetingWrites = params.writesPerSecond * windowSeconds; const conflictProbability = (1 - Math.exp(-expectedCompetingWrites)) * 100; return { conflictProbability };

outputs.label: Chance another write conflicts while yours is in flight
